title: Schema negotiator: enhanced diagnostics, tool exit signals, and streaming stability improvements
author: Priya Menon
description:
Context: Several customers reported intermittent structured-output failures when the model emitted partial JSON and then a tool returned a non-zero exit status. These manifested as confusing user-facing errors (invalid_schema) with no actionable signal from the tool layer. This PR introduces a schema negotiation helper plus richer diagnostics and an explicit mapping of tool exit signals into response-level error codes to improve debuggability and preserve streaming stability.

What this changes: Adds a Schema Negotiator component that runs at the start of response handling to record the requested response_format and normalize incoming schema hints. When a streaming chunk fails validation we now attach a compact diagnostic envelope (response_diagnostics) in the non-stream terminal event so callers can decide whether to fallback to soft-coercion, retry, or surface a hard error. We also standardize tool/function calling egress signals: tools that return non-zero exit codes are translated into structured tool_exit events with reason, code, and optional stderr snippet (truncated). The OpenAI compatibility shim now emits function_call -> tool_exit mapping so downstream SDKs see the same shape across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Design notes: The negotiator implements three phases: (1) handshake: normalize response_format (json_schema, structured, text) and register schema version; (2) runtime checks: lightweight streaming checkpoints validated against schema subsets to avoid full-parse on each token; (3) terminalization: assemble response_diagnostics if validation failed at any checkpoint and attach a stable resume_token. Checkpoints are spaced adaptively based on token velocity to avoid throughput regressions.

Compatibility: Kept OpenAI-compat layer intact but added a compatibility fallback header (x-rw-schema-hint) so older SDKs will ignore the new diagnostic envelope. Default behavior is non-breaking: strict_mode remains opt-in via response_format.strict=true.

Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests added for negotiator, checkpoints, and tool_exit mapping. Canary rollout plan: start on Hosted read-only workloads (non-customer facing) for 48hrs, then gate to 5% of customer traffic with automatic rollback on elevated invalid_schema rates.

Checklist: - [x] Schema negotiator implementation - [x] Checkpoint validation logic with adaptive spacing - [x] Diagnostic envelope (response_diagnostics) added to terminal events - [x] Tool exit mapping and OpenAI shim update - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Canary rollout plan

review_comments: Ethan Clarke: Please reduce allocations in the checkpoint hot path; allocating the full schema object per checkpoint will regress latency. Suggested: use a cached schema view.
Priya Menon: Updated to use SchemaView cache and added benchmark — micro-regression <1% on p50, p95 unaffected.
Rina Patel: Need clearer guidance in docs for SDKs that don't understand response_diagnostics; we should include example pseudocode for fallback.
Priya Menon: Added compatibility header x-rw-schema-hint and an SDK README snippet demonstrating soft-coercion fallback.
Marco Liu: CI flagged a race in tests on Linux runners — looks like a shared temp file. Please use unique temp dirs per test.
Priya Menon: Fixed test isolation, re-ran CI.
ci_summary: Initial CI run: failed (race in unit tests on Linux). Second run after fix: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, mypy/typed checks, benchmark smoke tests). Full test matrix passed on x86_64 Linux and macos-latest; rust streaming processor benchmarks within acceptable variance.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash-merge. PR message condensed into a single changelog entry; feature gated behind response_format.strict opt-in for immediate safety.
release_notes: Add Schema Negotiator and richer response_diagnostics for improved structured-output observability; map tool exit codes to structured tool_exit events. Default behavior unchanged unless response_format.strict is enabled. See docs/response_format.md for migration notes and canary instructions.
user_visible_changes: New terminal event field response_diagnostics (if validation failed) and tool_exit event objects emitted when tool returns non-zero. SDKs can opt-in to strict_mode via response_format.strict=true to enable hard schema enforcement.
rollback_plan: Canary rollout with automatic invalid_schema rate monitoring. If invalid_schema rate increases beyond 0.5% above baseline or latency p95 regresses >10ms on canary group, rollback to previous runtime binary and disable negotiator flag for traffic slice.
notes_for_ops: Enable additional debug logging at rw.schema=debug for one canary slice only. Diagnostic payloads are capped at 2KB to avoid exposure of large stderr blobs. Ensure observability alerting is wired to new metric rw.response_diagnostics.count.
docs_changes: docs/response_format.md updated with examples for response_diagnostics and SDK fallback pseudocode; compatibility section added describing x-rw-schema-hint header.
qa_signoff: QA verified checkpointing logic against long streaming sessions and tool exit translations; no data plane regressions observed in synthetic workloads.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps strict enforcement opt-in. Future follow-ups will add optional auto-coercion strategies and richer telemetry linking failing prompt examples to eval sets.
